title: Arterial blood gases: adult normal values and reading a result
applies: Adult values, as the source's own table is titled. A laboratory sets its own reference ranges, and your hospital's may differ.
written: Each card states figures from the cited page in Department Hub's own words. The page's text is not held here. The figures were read from the page by an AI assistant on the date given; 'twice' means two separate readings agreed, 'once' means there was a single reading.

cards.title: Normal arterial blood gas values
cards.answer: Adult normal arterial blood gas values: pH 7.35-7.45, PaO2 80-100 mmHg, PaCO2 35-45 mmHg, HCO3 22-26 mEq/L, SaO2 95-100%.

cards.title: Arterial pH
cards.answer: Adult normal arterial pH is 7.35-7.45. The source lists a pH less than 7.25 or greater than 7.60 as critical.

cards.title: PaO2
cards.answer: Adult normal PaO2 is 80-100 mmHg. The source lists a PaO2 less than 60 mmHg as critical.

cards.title: PaCO2
cards.answer: Adult normal PaCO2 is 35-45 mmHg. The source lists a PaCO2 less than 25 mmHg or greater than 60 mmHg as critical.

cards.title: HCO3 (bicarbonate)
cards.answer: Adult normal HCO3 is 22-26 mEq/L. The source lists an HCO3 less than 10 mEq/L or greater than 40 mEq/L as critical.

cards.title: SaO2 (arterial oxygen saturation)
cards.answer: Adult normal SaO2 is 95-100%. The source lists an SaO2 less than 88% as critical. SaO2 is measured from arterial blood; it is not the pulse-oximeter reading.

cards.title: Critical arterial blood gas values
cards.answer: Critical values in the source's adult table: pH less than 7.25 or greater than 7.60; PaO2 less than 60 mmHg; PaCO2 less than 25 mmHg or greater than 60 mmHg; HCO3 less than 10 mEq/L or greater than 40 mEq/L; SaO2 less than 88%.

cards.title: Acidosis or alkalosis, from the pH
cards.where: Table 15.5b, step 1, and the section text
cards.answer: A pH less than 7.35 is acidosis. A pH greater than 7.45 is alkalosis.

cards.title: Respiratory acidosis and respiratory alkalosis
cards.answer: The source calls it respiratory acidosis when the pH is less than 7.35 and the PaCO2 is greater than 45, and respiratory alkalosis when the pH is greater than 7.45 and the PaCO2 is less than 35.

cards.title: Metabolic acidosis and metabolic alkalosis
cards.answer: The source calls it metabolic acidosis when the pH is less than 7.35 and the HCO3 is less than 22, and metabolic alkalosis when the pH is greater than 7.45 and the HCO3 is greater than 26.

cards.title: Fully compensated, partially compensated, uncompensated
cards.answer: In the source's step 4: fully compensated means the pH is back to normal (7.35-7.45) while PaCO2 and HCO3 are both out of range. Partially compensated means the pH is still abnormal and PaCO2 and HCO3 are both abnormal. Uncompensated means the pH is abnormal and only one of PaCO2 or HCO3 is abnormal.

cards.title: Which value the lungs manage and which the kidneys
cards.answer: The source describes CO2 as an acid managed by the lungs and HCO3 as a base managed by the kidneys. As PaCO2 increases the pH decreases; as HCO3 increases the pH increases.
